text:
Connor Li: hey everyone :wave: I tried merging my personal kubeconfig with the company one and now `kubectl` is picking the wrong context. When I run `kubectl config get-contexts` I see two contexts with the same cluster name and conflicting user entries. Any tips?

Connor Li: I tried `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/work/reds-kubeconfig kubectl config view --merge --flatten` then wrote that to `~/.kube/merged` and pointed kubectl at it, but auth fails (401).

Connor Li: example of the user blocks in the merged file:```
users:
- name: admin@company
  user:
    auth-provider:
      name: oidc
      config:
        id-token: REDACTED
- name: dev-ci@company
  user:
    token: xxxxx
```

Connor Li: not sure which one kubectl is choosing.

DevEx Bot: Hi Connor — welcome! :tada: Quick checklist:
• run `kubectl config current-context` to see which context is active
• `kubectl config use-context <name>` will switch if the context exists
• If you have duplicate cluster names, rename contexts to be unique: `kubectl config rename-context old-name new-name`
• For a clean merge: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/work/reds-kubeconfig kubectl config view --merge --flatten > ~/.kube/merged && mv ~/.kube/merged ~/.kube/config` (backup first)

DevEx Bot: The 401 usually means the user entry in the kubeconfig doesn't match a valid credential (expired token / missing oidc refresh). If using OIDC make sure your `gcloud`/`aws-iam-authenticator`/browser auth flow completed.

Mira Patel: @Connor Li can you paste `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` output and `kubectl config view users` (omit tokens) here? I can check whether your user maps to the right RBAC group.

Connor Li: pasted below (tokens removed):```
contexts:
- dev-sandbox@dev-cluster
- dev-sandbox@dev-cluster-2
- ci-pipeline@dev-cluster

users:
- name: dev-ci@company
- name: connor.li@company (auth-provider: oidc)
```

Mira Patel: OK looks like `dev-sandbox@dev-cluster` and `dev-sandbox@dev-cluster-2` are different contexts pointing at different clusters but they share the same cluster shortname. Rename them to clarify: `kubectl config rename-context dev-sandbox@dev-cluster dev-sandbox-local` and `kubectl config rename-context dev-sandbox@dev-cluster-2 dev-sandbox-remote`. Then `kubectl use-context dev-sandbox-local` and try `kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=sandbox` to test permissions.

Mira Patel: If `kubectl auth can-i` says no, ping me and I can add a RoleBinding for `group:eng-onboarding` to `Role:dev-sandbox-reader` in the `sandbox` namespace.

Connor Li: tried rename + `kubectl use-context` — now `kubectl get pods -n sandbox` returns `error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)`.

Sam O'Neill: @Mira I can help with RBAC if you want. Connor, likely the oidc token didn't get refreshed for the merged config. Try removing the `users` section for `connor.li@company`, re-run the company login script at `https://auth.company.internal/login` (or run `company-auth login --refresh`) and then re-merge.

Connor Li: ok running the login script now. Thanks for the pointers — will report back in a few mins.

DevEx Bot: If you still see issues after refresh, post the output of `kubectl config view --minify --raw` (remove any secrets) and @mira or @sam will take a look. Also consider using `kubectl config set-cluster --server=<url>` only if endpoints differ.

Connor Li: login fixed it — `kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=sandbox` now returns yes. :relieved: Thanks all!

Mira Patel: Awesome — welcome aboard Connor :tada: If you'd like I can add a short doc to DevEx about common kubeconfig merge pitfalls.

Connor Li: would love that, thanks!
